21	channels, with an improvement of signiﬁcance up to 10%-20% when combined with boosted-top
22	tagging. Both the fully-hadronic and semi-leptonic channels yield comparable discovery potential

27	INTRODUCTION
28	The discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC has com-
29	pleted the particle content of the Standard Model (SM).
30	Precision measurements of the Higgs interaction to the
31	SM particles provides an excellent opportunity in under-
32	standing the nature of electroweak symmetry breaking
33	(EWSB) and in the search for new physics (NP) beyond
34	the SM. Among myriad possibilities, the large Yukawa
35	coupling of the top quark to the Higgs boson makes the
36	top quark one of the most interesting candles in search-
37	ing for NP underlying the EWSB. By the same token,
38	for the class of models addressing the naturalness of the
39	EWSB scale, it provides the most important window for
40	NP.
41	Some of these models often introduce new particles
42	which interact strongly to the top sector. Examples in-
43	clude two Higgs doublet models [1–3], left-right exten-
44	sions of the SM [4], models with a color-sextet or color-
45	octet [5–10], models with composite particles [11–32], etc.
46	NP that couples strongly to top quarks might manifest it-
47	self as heavy resonant states that can be produced at the
48	LHC. Therefore, searching for t¯t resonances at hadron
49	colliders is of particular importance. Experimental col-

291	def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
292	    """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.
293	
294	    Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
295	    dependency cycle.
296	    """
297	    names = {p.name for p in params}
298	    deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
299	    by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}
300	
301	    ordered: List[Parameter] = []
302	    emitted: set = set()
303	    remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order
304	
305	    while remaining:
306	        progressed = False
307	        still: List[str] = []
308	        for n in remaining:
309	            if deps[n] <= emitted:
310	                ordered.append(by_name[n])
311	                emitted.add(n)
312	                progressed = True
313	            else:
314	                still.append(n)
315	        remaining = still
316	        if not progressed:
317	            raise ValueError(
318	                f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
319	            )
320	    return ordered

2498	SUMMARY AND DISCUSSION
2499	With the discovery of Higgs boson at the LHC, the
2500	next highest priority is the precision measurement of the
2501	Higgs interaction with SM particles and searches for new
2502	phenomena beyond the SM. In both cases, the top quark
2503	plays a central role, making any searches associated with
2504	top quarks appealing.
2505	Among many others, a t¯t reso-
2506	nance is very well-motivated and searched for extensively
2507	at the LHC. Current bounds on the resonance mass lie
2508	in the TeV range, depending on models.
2509	In this paper we have studied a t¯t resonance that cou-
2510	ples primarily to top-quarks (top-philic), and very weakly
2511	to the rest of the SM particles. For concrete discussion,
2512	we have considered a case with a color singlet vector
2513	resonance, V1. In a simpliﬁed model, we have investi-
2514	gated the discovery potential of such a top-philic res-
2515	onance in the four-top ﬁnal state.
2516	In the large mass
2517	region (MV1 ≥1.5 TeV in our study), two tops from
2518	the decay of V1 are boosted and we have exploited the
2519	TOM with a new IR-safe template observable, template
2520	y-cut, to reconstruct the boosted top-quarks and reduce
2521	the dominant backgrounds. We combined jet trimming
2522	with TOM for the ﬁrst time to remove soft radiation thus
2523	further lowering the background rates.
2524	In our analysis we considered three diﬀerent channels:
2525	fully hadronic decay of all four top-quarks, semi-leptonic
2526	decay of the non-boosted tops with hadronic decays of
2527	boosted tops, and same-sign dileptonic decay. We found
2528	that the SSDL channel provides the best sensitivity, even
2529	though it suﬀers from small branching fractions, and the
2530	boosted-top tagging improved the signiﬁcance up to 10%-
2531	20% in the same sign dilepton channel.
2532	For example,
2533	we obtained S/
2534	√
2535	B = 5.6 for MV1 = 1.5 TeV and ct =
2536	2.0 without boosted techniques and an improvement to
2537	S/
2538	√
2539	B = 6.3 with boosted techniques at the 14 TeV HL-
2540	LHC. We found that the fully-hadronic and semi-leptonic
2541	channels show comparable signiﬁcances. This is due to
2542	the ty cut that we used to reduce the mis-tag rate of
2543	QCD jets, which shows a remarkable performance with
2544	the background reduction in the semi-leptonic channel.
2545	After combining all three channels we showed that the
2546	14 TeV LHC with 300 fb−1 can exclude such a top-philic
2547	resonance up to a coupling strength ct ≈2 for a resonance
2548	mass of 1.5 TeV and ct ≈3.4 for 2 TeV. The HL-LHC
2549	with 3000 fb−1 pushes down to ct ≈1 for 1.5 TeV and
2550	ct ≈2 for 2 TeV, respectively. Roughly our combined re-
2551	sults show about 60% (50%) reduction in the required lu-
2552	minosity for 2σ exclusion (5σ discovery), compared to the
2553	SSDL channel alone. The boosted top-tagging not only
2554	improves the sensitivity but also helps in reconstructing
2555	the mass of the top-philic resonance.
2556	Finally it is interesting to note that a light top-philic
2557	resonance (MV1 ≲300 GeV) can decay into diﬀerent ﬁ-
2558	nal states such as Zh (∼60%-80%), b¯b (∼20%-40%) or
2559	W +W −(a few % of branching fraction) [37]. Moreover
2560	the top-philic resonance may be a bridge to the dark sec-
2561	tor, through which dark matter can annihilate to the t¯t
2562	ﬁnal state. In this case, other collider signatures such
2563	as j + /ET and t¯t + /ET will open up. We show that a
2564	top-philic resonance provides a rich phenomenology at
2565	the LHC and hence encourage the experimental collabo-
2566	rations to pursue a dedicated study on it.

309	def render_model(model: FeynRulesModel) -> str:

313	    if model.interaction_order_hierarchy:

319	    if model.feynman_gauge is not None:

330	    if model.gauge_groups:

332	    if model.parameters:

334	        # particle's Mass/Width spec. Re-declaring them in M$Parameters makes the

337	        reserved = _reserved_mass_width_names(model.particles)
338	        params = [p for p in model.parameters

344	    for field, expr in model.gauge_xi:
345	        sections.append(f"GaugeXi[{field}] = {expr};")
346	
347	    for raw in model.raw_blocks:
348	        sections.append(raw)
349	
350	    for t in model.lagrangian_terms:
351	        op = ":=" if t.delayed else "="
352	        # Defensive: some (LLM-produced) expressions already carry a leading
353	        # assignment operator ("= ..." or ":= ..."); strip it so we don't emit a
354	        # duplicated operator (e.g. "L := := Block[...]").
355	        rhs = t.expression.lstrip()
356	        for lead in (":=", "="):
357	            if rhs.startswith(lead):
358	                rhs = rhs[len(lead):].lstrip()
359	                break
360	        sections.append(f"{t.name} {op} {rhs};")
361	
362	    env = Environment(
363	        loader=FileSystemLoader(_TEMPLATE_DIR),
364	        autoescape=select_autoescape(enabled_extensions=(), default=False),
365	        keep_trailing_newline=True,
366	    )
367	    template = env.get_template("model.fr.j2")
368	    return template.render(model_name=model.model_name, body="\n\n".join(sections))
